Migration finished. I found 38 remaining `db.query` call sites and migrated the 36 that are ours.

**Changed — 12 files, 36 call sites:**

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `admin/variantAdmin.js`, `repo/supplier.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `admin/macroAdmin.js`, `repo/sla.js` |

That brings first-party code to 75/75 files on `db.execute`.

**Two things I deliberately did not touch:**

1. **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js`** (2 sites) — still on `db.query`. Its header says *"Vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4. Do not edit — it is replaced wholesale on every upgrade, and local changes are silently lost."* Migrating it would be reverted by the next vendor bump, so this needs an upstream fix or a wrapper at the boundary. **This is the one loose end blocking removal of `db.query` from `lib/db.js`.**

2. **`cache.query(...)`** (25 sites) — `lib/cache.js` has its own unrelated `query(key)` method that takes a cache key, not SQL. Name collision only. A blanket find-replace on `.query(` would have silently broken every read-through cache lookup; I scoped the codemod to the literal `db.query(`.

**Verification** — I used a balanced-paren codemod rather than a regex, because the `update*` sites contain nested brackets (`patch[k]`) that a greedy pattern can mangle. Then:

- All 78 files pass `node --check`.
- Ran every exported function of all 12 files (18 getters, 12 listers, 12 updaters): 54 calls, all recorded as `form: 'execute'`, zero falling through to a shimmed `db.query`.
- Asserted `?`-placeholder count equals bound-param count at every site, and that the update path preserves param order (`['issued', 250, 'refund-9']`) — the case most at risk from the rewrite.
- Confirmed the cache path still works and `cache.query(key)` retains its semantics.
- Sanity-checked the harness against the vendor file to confirm it actually distinguishes `query` from `execute`, rather than passing vacuously.
- Normalized-diffed a migrated file against an already-migrated sibling: byte-identical, so the new code matches the earlier passes' style. All 225 `execute` sites share one canonical shape.

Scratch tooling removed; the tree is back to its original 78 files. Note `execute` also accepts a `timeoutMs` option — nothing needs it yet, but that's the capability the positional form couldn't carry.
